\[
I_{\text{out}}(x,y,c) = I(x,y,c) + \sigma\, n(x,y,c),
\qquad
n(x,y,c) \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\,1),
\qquad
\sigma = 10
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(I\): Input channel value
- \(I_{\text{out}}\): Output channel value before clipping and rounding
- \((x, y, c)\): Pixel position and channel
- \(n\): A standard normal random number
- \(\sigma\): Standard deviation of the noise in 8-bit levels

Every pixel and channel gets a value drawn from a normal distribution with mean 0 and standard deviation sigma. The values come from two uniform numbers through the Box-Muller transform. The uniform numbers depend only on the seed, the position and the channel. So a region gives the same noise as the whole image, and the same seed always gives the same result. Results outside 0 to 255 are clipped.
